tasks.short: Maintain accurate customer accounts across sales and customer records.

steps.what: Review new registrations and account changes in the {ECOMMERCE}.
Compare exports from the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM} in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve uncertain matches and conflicting details in the {CRM}.
Apply account changes and approved merges in the {CRM}.
Check incomplete records and failed updates in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure validation and account records in the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM}, adding a deterministic integration only where native synchronisation falls short. Stable identifiers permit routine updates; uncertain identity matches enter an exception queue, and merges require recorded approval before execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate identifiers, unclear field ownership and fragile exports made synchronisation expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation and import features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mapping, retry and reconciliation code.
tasks.still_hard: Shared addresses, guest purchases and conflicting contact details remain difficult. GDPR purpose, retention and access requirements constrain which records may be linked.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real duplicate from different people sharing contact details, and decide when evidence is insufficient.

ambition.what: Customer account continuity across guest purchases and registered accounts, after identity verification.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying records to resolving identity exceptions and preventing recurring data faults. Merge and access rights remain limited to the approved mandate.

reach.task: Prepare eligible customer segments for campaigns.
reach.learn: Learn consent provenance, suppression rules and the difference between account identity and marketing eligibility.

evidence.claim: Customer account validation, controlled imports and exception queues can usually be implemented without a model.
The proposed step shares, residual effort and delivery ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The reference company uses separate customer records in the {ECOMMERCE} and {CRM}; a single master system would remove the comparison step.
Account data is mainly structured, consistent with the supplied prior; ambiguous identity decisions remain human.
The write gate applies to merges and disputed corrections. Validated routine updates run under configured rules.
Delivery ranges are working-day estimates for one account flow and may overlap.
The access estimate includes privacy review and any employee consultation required by national rules if working practices change.
unknowns: Which system owns each account field and identifier.
Whether native synchronisation, reliable APIs and change logs are available.
Actual duplicate rates, guest-account volumes and exception handling time.
Approved retention rules, merge rights and permitted uses of customer data.
research_questions: Can native synchronisation replace the export comparison entirely?
Which matching rules pass a labelled sample without false merges?
Can failed updates be replayed without duplicating or overwriting newer changes?
new_work: Review uncertain matches and approve merges.
Maintain field ownership and validation rules.
Investigate synchronisation failures and audit account changes.
Test mappings when account schemas change.

tasks.short: Promote products through communities, marketing messages and online advertising.

steps.what: Select products, audiences and offers using the {ECOMMERCE} and {BI}.
Write channel copy and adapt approved assets in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Campaign brief, approved product facts, reusable assets and channel constraints.
loop.output: Channel copy with product claims linked to approved facts.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates, links and length mechanically; a person checks claims, tone and community fit.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per channel; unsupported claims or failed checks return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover recurring offers, but varied products and community contexts require limited language adaptation.

steps.what: Build campaign audiences and exclusions in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} and {ADS}.
Review claims, audience, spending and timing in the {DOCS}.
Publish approved posts, send campaigns and activate advertising.
Compare delivery, engagement and sales results across channel screens.
Answer community responses and discuss product use through the {SOCIAL}.

tasks.design: Use approved facts in the {DOCS} for bounded copy drafting, and configure audiences, exclusions, scheduling and budget limits in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {SOCIAL} and {ADS}. Publication requires approval of the exact content and settings; a deterministic feed into the {BI} tracks results while the merchant handles community conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel formats differed, approvals travelled separately from campaign settings, and performance data needed manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling and segmentation already handle routine execution. Bounded drafting and faster integration development reduce preparation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Community trust, persuasive positioning and reliable attribution remain difficult. GDPR, EU AI Act obligations where applicable, and national electronic-marketing rules must be reflected in the chosen use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when promotion is unwelcome, judge whether a claim is credible and respond candidly to customers.

ambition.what: Weekly creative allocation decisions using contribution margin and audience fatigue.

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time formatting and scheduling, and more time testing offers and speaking with customers. Within a delegated budget, they can recommend weekly reallocations; approval limits remain explicit.

reach.task: Allocate campaign spending between audiences and creative variants.
reach.learn: Learn incrementality, contribution margin and frequency effects before changing allocations.

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick supports product-description generation; this supports the bounded drafting component, not autonomous campaign management.
Scheduling, audience exclusions and budget limits can often be configured in existing channel systems.
The proposed effort shares and build ranges are estimates; the digest provides no measured case for this complete workflow.

assumptions: The merchant operates several channels with reusable product facts and assets.
Actual publishing and community work occur mainly in channel screens; the supplied mail share overstates mailbox work for this decomposition.
Approval binds to a fixed content and settings version; material changes invalidate it.
The final conversation step is performed directly by a person under an existing response mandate.
Build estimates cover one language and a limited set of channels; media production and advertising spend are excluded.
Access work includes privacy review and any consultation required by national rules if employee-level monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which channels permit native scheduling or API publication.
Who may approve claims, targeting and spending.
Available consent records, suppression rules and audience restrictions.
Whether sales results can be joined to campaign data at an appropriate aggregation level.
Number of languages, creative formats and weekly campaigns.
research_questions: Which recurring campaign formats can use fixed templates without a model?
Can approval remain bound to the exact campaign version across every channel?
Which outcome measure distinguishes profitable sales from attributed clicks?
new_work: Review draft claims and channel suitability.
Maintain product facts, templates and suppression rules.
Handle rejected publications, broken links and delivery failures.
Audit spending limits and investigate attribution discrepancies.

tasks.short: Coordinate shopping-search placements with search marketing specialists.

steps.what: Gather product availability and placement results from the {ECOMMERCE} and {ADS}.
Prepare a placement brief in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated placement metrics, product constraints and the merchant's campaign objectives.
loop.output: A placement brief separating facts, requested changes and open questions.
loop.check: Populate figures deterministically; verify every narrative claim against supplied inputs and review priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing objectives or unsupported conclusions return to the merchant.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed report covers metrics, but connecting varied commercial objectives to specialist questions needs limited drafting.

steps.what: Discuss placement trade-offs and agree priorities with the search marketing strategist.
Record owners, deadlines and agreed settings in the {PROJECT}.
Apply agreed feed and placement settings in the {ADS}.
Verify feed acceptance and placement outcomes in the {ADS}.

tasks.design: Join the {ECOMMERCE} and {ADS} data into a validated baseline, and generate a bounded placement brief in the {DOCS}. Capture agreed settings in structured fields in the {PROJECT}, configure their execution in the {ADS}, and require specialist approval before activation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Merchandising goals, feed errors and advertising results were held separately. Free-text requests forced specialists to clarify settings repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured requests, native feed checks and inexpensive integration code remove much of the coordination work. A small drafting loop can prepare the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Placement availability, auctions and platform policies limit control. The merchant and specialist still need to balance margin, visibility and learning.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate priorities with the specialist and recognise when a commercially attractive request is technically unrealistic.

ambition.what: Weekly placement reprioritisation using stock risk and contribution margin.

tasks.altitude: The merchant arrives at specialist discussions with validated evidence and explicit trade-offs. They can propose priorities more often; specialist activation rights and spending limits remain explicit.

reach.task: Diagnose shopping-feed exclusions and assess placement changes.
reach.learn: Learn feed eligibility, auction mechanics and how to separate rejection from weak bidding performance.

evidence.claim: Feed validation, structured change requests and status reporting are suitable for configuration or deterministic integration.
The digest contains no directly documented shopping-placement collaboration case; automation and effort estimates remain E1.

assumptions: The task includes the specialist handoff and verification, so step shares represent combined task effort.
Agreed settings are captured in structured fields during the discussion, avoiding automated interpretation of meeting recordings.
Routine changes use supported configuration; novel bidding or placement strategy remains specialist work.
The desired online location is a commercial objective, not a guaranteed placement.
Access estimates include agency permissions where relevant and consultation under national rules if staff monitoring is added.
unknowns: Whether the specialist is internal or external.
Available feed, placement and performance interfaces.
The merchant's budget mandate and the specialist's activation authority.
Which status checks are already automated.
Whether placement and margin data share stable product identifiers.
research_questions: Can native feeds and diagnostics satisfy the requirement without custom integration?
Which placement requests are precise enough to execute from structured fields?
How quickly can accepted settings be distinguished from actual placement outcomes?
new_work: Review generated briefs and maintain request fields.
Approve activation and handle unsupported settings.
Investigate feed rejections and delayed results.
Maintain product mappings and specialist access.

tasks.short: Assess product and market opportunities before proposing merchandising tests.

steps.what: Define the opportunity question and decision criteria in the {DOCS}.
Analyse category sales, returns and search demand in the {BI}.
Read market reports and competitor pages from research sources in {OTHER}.

loop.input: A bounded set of accessible reports and pages selected for the research brief.
loop.output: An evidence register with claims, exact source passages, dates, units and missing information.
loop.check: Require a retrievable passage for every claim; check dates and units, flag conflicting sources and sample extractions.
loop.stop: Process at most 20 documents per run with one retry each; inaccessible or conflicting evidence goes to manual research.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds should be used first, but relevant reports and pages express comparable facts in varied prose.

steps.what: Calculate margin, demand and stock scenarios in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Write an opportunity recommendation and test proposal in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence, computed scenarios, decision criteria and unresolved gaps.
loop.output: A recommendation draft with alternatives, assumptions and a proposed test.
loop.check: Link factual claims to the evidence register; import calculations unchanged and have the merchant assess the recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence produces an explicit gap, and weak recommendations return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies the structure, but explaining conflicting evidence and uncertainty needs bounded language synthesis.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions and decide whether to authorise the merchandising test.

tasks.design: Configure category baselines in the {BI}, extract cited evidence from a fixed research pack into the {DOCS}, and calculate viability scenarios deterministically on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A second bounded loop drafts the recommendation from reviewed evidence; the marketing manager approves the test decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research mixed browsing, inconsistent cost assumptions and bespoke spreadsheets. Evidence and calculations were difficult to refresh together.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data extracts and scenario code make recurring analysis cheaper. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce reading and writing effort without inventing missing market data.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor demand, future customer behaviour and supplier reliability are often unobservable. Source licensing, comparability and uncertain cost inputs can dominate the effort.
tasks.human_edge: Identify a useful commercial question, notice misleading evidence and design a cheap test that could disprove the opportunity.

ambition.what: Fortnightly selection of one product hypothesis for a limited merchandising test.

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time collecting figures and more time testing assumptions with customers and suppliers. With a delegated test budget, they could authorise small experiments; larger commitments remain with the budget holder.

reach.task: Design and interpret a product-demand validation study.
reach.learn: Learn sampling bias, research design and how to distinguish stated interest from willingness to buy.

evidence.claim: Scenario calculations and category baselines can be deterministic; extracting heterogeneous prose may benefit from bounded model use.
The digest reports a case of fabricated sources in an AI-assisted report, supporting explicit source verification.
No digest case establishes the proposed merchant productivity gains or opportunity-selection quality; delivery and effort figures are estimates.

assumptions: Recurring category research is common enough to justify reusable baselines and scenarios.
The source pack is selected by a person or a fixed source register; open-ended autonomous browsing is unnecessary.
Demand inputs are scenarios rather than validated forecasts.
The approval concerns a test plan; purchasing and advertising execution require their own action controls.
Build estimates cover one category and existing licensed sources; new research subscriptions and primary research are excluded.
Access work covers GDPR review for customer data and any consultation required by national rules if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Available category, return, search and contribution-margin data.
Rights to retrieve, retain and process external research sources.
Typical research volume and cost of obtaining missing evidence.
Who can approve tests and what budget could be delegated.
Whether product costs include returns, fulfilment, duties and markdown exposure.
research_questions: Which decisions recur enough to use the same evidence and scenario template?
How often do extracted claims retain their meaning after dates, units and market scope are checked?
Which low-cost test best distinguishes demand uncertainty from weak merchandising execution?
new_work: Review evidence passages, contradictions and source freshness.
Maintain cost assumptions and scenario definitions.
Update connectors and extraction checks when sources change.
Compare approved test predictions with outcomes and revise the research approach.

role.altitude: The merchant's week shifts toward product tests, commercial trade-offs and customer conversations. Wider budget or assortment rights require an explicit mandate; automation alone grants none.
reach: Search marketing strategist: diagnose feed exclusions and assess placement economics.
Market research analyst: design credible product-demand tests.
Advertising and promotions manager: recommend spending changes using incremental contribution.
skills_to_grow: Customer identity, consent and data-quality controls.
Structured campaign briefs and specialist collaboration.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small merchandising experiment programme that connects customer feedback, market evidence, product availability and campaign economics, with delegated test limits and explicit approval for larger commitments.
